concepts.title: Peiligang: Early Shamanism and Personal Charisma
concepts.excerpt: Peiligang culture (8,000-7,000 BCE) was one of the earliest Neolithic societies in the Yellow River valley.

concepts.title: Hongshan: Ritual Landscape and the Materialization of Power
concepts.excerpt: Hongshan culture (5,000-3,000 BCE) occupied the Liaodong Peninsula in northeast China, contemporary with and adjacent to the Yangshao culture to the south.

concepts.title: Longshan: Oracle Bones and the Formalization of Divination
concepts.excerpt: The Longshan culture (3,000-1,900 BCE) marks a turning point in the relationship between shamanism and state authority: the formalization of divination into a standardized protocol.

concepts.title: Taosi: Astronomy as State Apparatus
concepts.excerpt: Taosi is a prehistoric walled city in the Yellow River valley, dated to approximately 2,600-2,000 BCE (Longshan culture).

concepts.title: Carnac Stones: Processional Knowledge Architecture
concepts.excerpt: The Carnac stones in Brittany are not a single monument. They are 3,000 individual menhirs—standing stones—arranged in 11 parallel rows extending for 4 kilometers across the landscape.

concepts.title: Chaco Canyon Great Houses: Astronomical Knowledge Engineering
concepts.excerpt: Chaco Canyon in New Mexico contains approximately 15 Great Houses—massive ceremonial structures built between 900-1150 CE.

concepts.title: Grooved Ware Societies: Settlement Transition Evidence
concepts.excerpt: Grooved ware is a pottery type appearing in the archaeological record around 3000-2400 BCE across Britain and Orkney.

concepts.title: Orkney Carved Stone Balls: Portable-Monumental Hybrids
concepts.excerpt: These objects are not tools. They have no practical function for hunting, gathering, or food preparation.

concepts.title: West Kennet Long Barrow: Genealogical Architecture
concepts.excerpt: Unlike Newgrange, West Kennet was not designed for solar alignment. Instead, it was designed as a genealogical archive.

concepts.title: Plains of Jars: Iron Age Cemetery or Ritual Landscape? When Material Evidence Outlasts Its Meaning
concepts.excerpt: Imagine walking across a high plateau and encountering thousands of enormous stone jars—some taller than a person, carved from single blocks of stone, scattered across the landscape in seemingly random clusters.

concepts.title: Prehistoric Fortifications: Foragers & Farmers in Violent Contact
concepts.excerpt: Dominant 20th-century archaeology constructed a story: hunters are peaceful, agriculture brings war.

concepts.title: Shamanism & Chinese State: 7,000 Years of Power Consolidation
concepts.excerpt: Chinese civilization did not emerge from chaos to order in a single moment.

concepts.title: Aztec Metaphysics — Teotl, Olin, and the Violence of Creation
concepts.excerpt: Before we say "Aztec human sacrifice was brutal and primitive," consider that the Aztecs had a fully worked-out answer to the question of why the universe exists and what keeps it running — an answer that made human sacrifice not a sign of bloodlust but a logical necessity, the way paying your electricity bill is a logical necessity if you want the lights to stay on.

concepts.title: Snake Mythology: Venom as Invisible Threat and Cosmic Principle
concepts.excerpt: Snakes occupy a remarkable position in world mythology. They appear not merely as animals but as cosmic principles—forces that shape creation, chaos, and transformation.

concepts.title: Tuunbaq: Predator Mythology and Environmental Terror
concepts.excerpt: Tuunbaq appears in Inuit mythology as a powerful predatory entity—a creature of the Arctic that hunts, kills, and cannot be defeated through ordinary means.
